# [USBD05] Relational Model Instantiation in Oracle

* **Priority:** High
* **Story Points:** 5
* **Module / Component:** `Database` / `Oracle DDL + Data Population`
* **Status:** Draft

---

## 👤 User Story Description

**As a** Product Owner, **I want** the relational model to be instantiated in an Oracle RDBMS using the SQL DDL code generated by an appropriate tool, **so that** the database exists, is populated with data and allows verifying that the model fulfills the requirements.

---

## 🚦 Definition of Ready (DoR)

* [ ] **Clear User Story:** Story follows the standard *As a / I want to / So that* format.
* [ ] **Acceptance Criteria Defined:** Clear, testable ACs agreed upon by Product and Engineering.
* [ ] **Dependencies Identified:** [USBD04] logical model is approved and available.
* [ ] **Inputs/Outputs Mapped:** Required scripts, sample data and expected results are documented.
* [ ] **Estimation Complete:** Story has been refined and estimated (story points assigned) by the dev team.
* [ ] **Small & Actionable:** Story is scoped down enough to be completed within a single sprint.

---

## 💬 Customer Specifications & Clarifications

* **Clarification:** The DDL code must be generated by an appropriate tool (e.g., a modelling tool or an LLM) from the logical model defined in [USBD04].
* **Clarification:** **All** tables must contain data; no table may be left empty.
* **Clarification:** The inserted data must allow verifying that the model fulfills the requirements.
* **Clarification:** The result will be demonstrated on **Oracle FreeSQL**.
* **Out of Scope:** Design of the logical model and ER diagram (see [USBD04]); application code.

---

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] **AC1 - DDL Instantiation:** The relational model is instantiated in Oracle using the SQL DDL code generated by an appropriate tool, creating all tables and constraints without errors.
* [ ] **AC2 - Populated Tables:** All tables in the database are populated with data.
* [ ] **AC3 - Requirements Verification:** The inserted data allows verifying that the model fulfills the requirements (valid data accepted, relationships consistent).
* [ ] **AC4 - Demonstration:** The solution is shown on Oracle FreeSQL.

---

## 🔒 Non-Functional Requirements & Security

* **Reproducibility (NFR1):** The script can be executed from scratch on an empty schema, in the correct order (create → insert), without errors.
* **Integrity (NFR2):** Data is loaded in an order that respects the foreign key dependencies (parent tables before child tables), without disabling or deferring any constraint.

---

## 🔗 Found Out Dependencies

### Upstream Dependencies (Required before starting)
* **[USBD04] Relational Model (Logical Level):** provides the model from which the DDL code is generated.

### Downstream Dependencies (Impacted by this story)

* **Application:** uses the instantiated and populated database.

---

## Edge Cases

* **Insertion Order:** Child tables are populated only after their parent tables (foreign keys).
* **Constraint Violations:** Data violating PK, FK, UNIQUE, NOT NULL or CHECK is rejected.
* **Empty Table:** A table without data is considered a failure of AC2.
* **Platform Differences:** Syntax not supported by Oracle FreeSQL is adjusted and documented.
